The longest river in the world is the Nile River.

In the provided text, the central conflict arises from the clash between economic greed and cultural preservation. Jacob, a prospector, faces an internal moral dilemma as he discovers gold on land that is sacred to the local indigenous tribe. This external discovery triggers an external conflict with the tribe's chief, who is determined to protect his people's heritage from exploitation. The situation escalates when outsiders become aware of the gold, forcing Jacob to choose between his personal gain and his loyalty to the indigenous community, highlighting the tension between individual ambition and collective rights.
